metadata.research_notes: Comprehensive local crawl of Geth repository (commit b98b255) including core execution layer components, Engine API implementation, transaction pool architecture, block building workflow, and EIP implementations. Web research attempted for official Ethereum execution specs and Geth documentation portals. Analysis covers mainnet configuration with fork activation through Osaka and BPO2. [S1] [S2] [S3] Sources: [S1] /README.md, [S2] /params/config.go, [S3] /params/protocol_params.go

trusted_entities.assumption: The execution client trusts authenticated Engine API calls from a paired consensus client to provide canonical fork choice views via engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV1/V2/V3 and valid payload construction requests via engine_newPayloadV1/V2/V3. [S4] [S5] The Engine API is registered with the Authenticated: true flag, requiring JWT-based authentication for all requests. [S4] Sources: [S4] /eth/catalyst/api.go:48-58, [S5] /beacon/engine/types.go:31-53
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: A malicious or compromised consensus client could inject invalid payload attributes leading to construction of non-canonical blocks, cause liveness failures by providing incorrect fork choice state, trigger invalid state transitions, or cause the execution client to build on invalid parent blocks. This breaks the fundamental trust boundary between EL and CL post-merge. [S4] Sources: [S4] /eth/catalyst/api.go

trusted_entities.entity: Local ChainConfig and Fork Activation Parameters
trusted_entities.assumption: Node operators trust locally configured chain parameters in params/config.go (fork block numbers, timestamps, terminal total difficulty, deposit contract address, blob schedule configuration) to match network consensus. [S2] [S6] Configuration includes activation times for Shanghai (1681338455), Cancun (1710338135), Prague (1746612311), Osaka (1764798551), BPO1 (1765290071), BPO2 (1767747671) on mainnet. [S2] Sources: [S2] /params/config.go:43-76, [S6] /params/config.go:1-27
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Incorrect fork activation configuration causes nodes to diverge from network consensus, reject valid transactions (e.g., blob transactions before Cancun activation recognized locally), construct invalid blocks with wrong EIP rules applied, or accept invalid blocks that violate active network rules. Results in chain split and loss of consensus. [S2] [S7] Sources: [S2] /params/config.go, [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go:75-94

trusted_entities.assumption: The execution layer trusts hardcoded system contract addresses and bytecode for EIP-4788 BeaconRootsAddress (0x000F3df6D732807Ef1319fB7B8bB8522d0Beac02), EIP-2935 HistoryStorageAddress (0x0000F90827F1C53a10cb7A02335B175320002935), EIP-7002 WithdrawalQueueAddress (0x00000961Ef480Eb55e80D19ad83579A64c007002), and EIP-7251 ConsolidationQueueAddress (0x0000BBdDc7CE488642fb579F8B00f3a590007251) as deployed with specific bytecode matching protocol specifications. [S8] System transactions are sent from SystemAddress (0xfffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffffe) with 30M gas limit. [S9] [S10] Sources: [S8] /params/protocol_params.go:204-221, [S9] /core/state_processor.go:220-242, [S10] /core/state_processor.go:244-272
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: If system contract addresses or bytecode differ from network consensus, beacon block roots will not be stored correctly (breaking EIP-4788 oracles), historical block hashes will be unavailable (breaking EIP-2935 BLOCKHASH extension), execution layer triggered withdrawals will fail (breaking EIP-7002), and validator consolidations will fail (breaking EIP-7251). This breaks cross-layer protocol functionality and validator operations. [S8] [S9] Sources: [S8] /params/protocol_params.go, [S9] /core/state_processor.go

trusted_entities.assumption: The execution client trusts that peer nodes on the p2p network propagate well-formed transactions and blocks, though all content is validated before acceptance. [S1] Transaction pool validation performs stateless checks (signature, nonce limits, gas limits, intrinsic gas, fee caps) before admission. [S7] [S11] Block validation verifies parent linkage, state transitions, gas usage, and consensus rules. [S12] Sources: [S1] /README.md:162-200, [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go:61-154, [S11] /core/txpool/validation.go:1-31, [S12] /core/block_validator.go
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Malicious peers can attempt DoS via invalid transactions (rejected by validation), cause resource exhaustion via large or expensive transactions (mitigated by gas limits and mempool policies), or propagate invalid blocks (rejected by block validation). However, stateless validation prevents most attacks, and EIP-1559 base fee plus priority fee requirements limit spam. Blob pool has additional DoS protections with higher replacement bumps (100% vs 10%) and per-account limits. [S13] [S14] Sources: [S13] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go:164-200, [S14] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go:74-86

trusted_entities.entity: KZG Cryptographic Setup and Blob Verification
trusted_entities.assumption: For EIP-4844 blob transactions, the execution layer trusts the KZG trusted setup parameters used for blob commitment verification (kzg4844.VerifyBlobProof for legacy proofs, validateBlobSidecarOsaka for post-Osaka cell proofs). [S15] [S16] Blob transactions must include valid KZG commitments, proofs matching blob data, and commitment hashes in transaction. [S15] Sidecar version distinguishes proof types (version 1 for Osaka cell proofs, version 0 for legacy). [S17] Sources: [S15] /core/txpool/validation.go:157-200, [S16] /crypto/kzg4844/kzg4844.go, [S17] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go:110-133
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: If KZG trusted setup is compromised or verification logic is flawed, invalid blob data could be accepted as valid, breaking data availability guarantees for L2 rollups. This would allow forged rollup commitments and compromise L2 security. However, the trusted setup is a one-time ceremony with broad participation, and verification logic follows EIP-4844 specification. [S15] Sources: [S15] /core/txpool/validation.go

trusted_entities.assumption: The execution layer trusts implementations of precompiled contracts (ecrecover at 0x01, sha256 at 0x02, ripemd160 at 0x03, identity at 0x04, modexp at 0x05, bn256Add at 0x06, bn256ScalarMul at 0x07, bn256Pairing at 0x08, blake2f at 0x09, bls12381 operations at 0x0a-0x0f, point evaluation at 0x0a for EIP-4844, secp256r1 verify at 0x100 for EIP-7212) to match protocol specifications. [S18] Gas costs are defined in protocol_params.go. [S3] Sources: [S18] /core/vm/contracts.go, [S3] /params/protocol_params.go:140-168
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Incorrect precompile implementations cause consensus failures as different nodes compute different results for the same input. This breaks state root agreement and causes permanent chain splits. Precompile gas cost errors allow DoS (underpriced) or waste user funds (overpriced). Cryptographic precompile errors (ecrecover, bn256, bls12381, point evaluation) break signature verification, ZK proof verification, and blob commitments. [S18] Sources: [S18] /core/vm/contracts.go

trusted_entities.entity: Local State Database and Disk Storage
trusted_entities.assumption: The execution client trusts the integrity of its local state database (LevelDB/Pebble), trie structures, and persistent storage containing account state, contract storage, block history, and transaction receipts. [S1] Database corruption detection relies on state root verification and trie consistency checks. [S1] Sources: [S1] /README.md:54-69, [S19] /ethdb/
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Database corruption leads to incorrect state root calculations, inability to validate blocks, potential acceptance of invalid transactions, or failure to construct valid blocks. Trie corruption prevents state access and block execution. Recovery requires resync from genesis or trusted snapshot. Node operators must ensure filesystem and disk reliability. [S1] Sources: [S1] /README.md

trusted_entities.assumption: Geth trusts the Go 1.23+ runtime, standard library cryptographic implementations (especially crypto/ecdsa for transaction signatures), and external dependencies including holiman/uint256 for 256-bit arithmetic, secp256k1 for signature operations, and kzg4844 for blob proof verification. [S1] [S20] Sources: [S1] /README.md:20, [S20] /go.mod
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Runtime or cryptographic library vulnerabilities could allow signature forgery (compromising transaction authentication), arbitrary code execution, memory corruption, or incorrect EVM execution. Supply chain attacks on dependencies could inject malicious code. Mitigation relies on Go team security, dependency auditing, and reproducible builds. [S1] Sources: [S1] /README.md

trusted_entities.entity: EIP-1559 Base Fee and Blob Fee Markets
trusted_entities.assumption: The execution layer trusts EIP-1559 base fee calculation (consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go CalcBaseFee function) and EIP-4844 blob fee calculation (consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go CalcExcessBlobGas and fakeExponential) to implement protocol-specified market mechanisms correctly. [S21] [S22] Base fee updates use elasticity multiplier (2) and change denominator (8). [S21] [S23] Blob fee uses exponential pricing based on excess blob gas. [S22] Sources: [S21] /consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go:56-98, [S22] /consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:45-227, [S23] /params/protocol_params.go:133-135
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Incorrect fee calculations cause consensus failures as nodes disagree on valid base fee or blob fee values, leading to block rejection and chain splits. Fee market manipulation could make transactions permanently underpriced (DoS) or overpriced (unusable network). Exponential blob fee calculation errors affect L2 rollup economics. [S21] [S22] Sources: [S21] /consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go, [S22] /consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go

trusted_entities.entity: Transaction Signature Validation and Signer Recovery
trusted_entities.assumption: The execution layer trusts transaction signature validation and sender recovery (types.Sender function using configured signer for fork-appropriate signature schemes: Frontier, Homestead, EIP-155, EIP-2930, EIP-1559, EIP-4844) to correctly authenticate transaction origin. [S7] [S24] Nonce limits enforced per EIP-2681 (nonce < 2^64-1). [S7] Sources: [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go:116-122, [S24] /core/types/transaction_signing.go
trusted_entities.impact_if_compromised: Signature validation failures allow unauthorized spending of funds (signature forgery), replay attacks across chains (if EIP-155 chain ID not enforced), or acceptance of transactions with invalid signatures. Sender recovery errors attribute transactions to wrong accounts, breaking account state and nonce ordering. This is a critical security boundary. [S7] Sources: [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go

user_flows.title: Legacy Transaction Submission and Pool Admission (EIP-155, pre-EIP-1559)
preconditions: Node is synced and JSON-RPC HTTP/WS/IPC interface is enabled with eth API. [S1] [S25] Sources: [S1] /README.md:176-189, [S25] /eth/api_backend.go
steps: 1. RPC client submits signed legacy transaction via eth_sendRawTransaction with RLP-encoded tx bytes. [S25] Sources: [S25] /internal/ethapi/api.go
2. RPC handler decodes transaction and performs initial format validation (RLP structure, signature format). [S25] Sources: [S25] /internal/ethapi/api.go
3. Transaction pool receives tx and invokes stateless validation via ValidateTransaction. [S7] Sources: [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go:61-154

4. Validation checks: (a) transaction type supported by pool (legacy tx type 0x0 always supported), (b) transaction size under MaxSize limit, (c) gas limit does not exceed current head block gas limit, (d) gas fee cap and tip cap under 256 bits, (e) fee cap >= tip cap, (f) signature verification and sender recovery, (g) nonce under 2^64-1 limit per EIP-2681, (h) intrinsic gas satisfied (21000 base + calldata costs), (i) gas tip cap meets pool minimum tip requirement. [S7] Sources: [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go:61-154

5. If stateless validation passes, transaction is checked against current state: (a) sender account balance sufficient for value + gas * gasPrice, (b) sender nonce matches or is future nonce (with gap limits), (c) transaction not already in pool. [S26] Sources: [S26] /core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go

6. Transaction is inserted into legacy pool pending queue (if nonce matches current) or future queue (if nonce is gap). [S26] Pool enforces per-account transaction limits and global pool limits. [S26] Sources: [S26] /core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go

7. If transaction is pending (executable), it is announced to connected peers via transaction hash announcement. [S27] Full transaction body is sent only upon peer request (pull model). [S27] Sources: [S27] /eth/handler.go

8. Transaction remains in pool until included in block, replaced by higher fee transaction (10% bump required), or evicted due to pool limits or staleness. [S26] Sources: [S26] /core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go
postconditions: Transaction is admitted to mempool with status pending or future, made available for block building, and propagated to network if executable. [S26] [S27] Sources: [S26] /core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go, [S27] /eth/handler.go

user_flows.title: EIP-1559 Dynamic Fee Transaction Submission (Type 0x2)
preconditions: Network has activated London fork (EIP-1559) and node configuration reflects this. [S2] Current block header includes base fee field. [S21] Sources: [S2] /params/config.go:57, [S21] /consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go
steps: 1. RPC client submits signed EIP-1559 transaction (type 0x2) via eth_sendRawTransaction with fields: chainId, nonce, maxPriorityFeePerGas, maxFeePerGas, gasLimit, to, value, data, accessList, v, r, s. [S25] Sources: [S25] /internal/ethapi/api.go
2. RPC handler decodes and validates transaction format. [S25] Sources: [S25] /internal/ethapi/api.go

3. ValidateTransaction performs stateless checks including: (a) type 0x2 accepted after London fork, (b) size under limit, (c) maxFeePerGas >= maxPriorityFeePerGas, (d) gas limit reasonable, (e) signature valid, (f) intrinsic gas calculation includes access list costs (2400 gas per address + 1900 per storage key per EIP-2930), (g) maxPriorityFeePerGas meets pool minimum. [S7] [S28] Sources: [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go:61-154, [S28] /params/protocol_params.go:99-100

4. Effective gas price computed as effectiveTip = min(maxFeePerGas - baseFee, maxPriorityFeePerGas). [S29] Transaction must satisfy maxFeePerGas >= baseFee to be valid for current block. [S29] Sources: [S29] /miner/ordering.go
5. State-dependent validation checks sender balance covers value + gasLimit * maxFeePerGas and nonce correctness. [S26] Sources: [S26] /core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go

6. Transaction inserted into legacy pool pending/future queues with sorting by effective tip for miner selection. [S26] [S29] Sources: [S26] /core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go, [S29] /miner/ordering.go
7. Transaction announced to peers and made available for inclusion in next block. [S27] Sources: [S27] /eth/handler.go
8. Replacement requires 10% bump in both maxFeePerGas and maxPriorityFeePerGas. [S26] Sources: [S26] /core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go
postconditions: EIP-1559 transaction admitted to pool, sorted by effective tip, ready for block building with base fee burn mechanism applied during execution. [S26] [S29] Sources: [S26] /core/txpool/legacypool/legacypool.go, [S29] /miner/ordering.go

user_flows.title: EIP-4844 Blob Transaction Submission and Validation (Type 0x3)
preconditions: Network has activated Cancun fork (EIP-4844). [S2] Blob pool is enabled. [S13] Client has blob transaction with attached sidecar (blobs, commitments, proofs). [S15] Sources: [S2] /params/config.go:62, [S13] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go, [S15] /core/txpool/validation.go:157-200
steps: 1. L2 sequencer submits blob transaction (type 0x3) via eth_sendRawTransaction with transaction body and sidecar containing blobs (up to 6 blobs per tx), KZG commitments, and proofs (legacy KZG proofs or Osaka cell proofs depending on version). [S15] [S17] Sources: [S15] /core/txpool/validation.go:157-200, [S17] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go:110-133

2. ValidateTransaction performs blob-specific checks: (a) type 0x3 accepted after Cancun, (b) transaction size under txMaxSize (1MB), (c) blob count under maxBlobsPerTx (6), (d) sidecar present, (e) blobGasFeeCap >= BlobTxMinBlobGasprice (1 wei), (f) number of blobs matches commitments and proofs, (g) commitment hashes match transaction blobHashes field, (h) KZG proof verification (VerifyBlobProof for each blob for legacy, validateBlobSidecarOsaka for Osaka). [S15] [S14] [S30] Sources: [S15] /core/txpool/validation.go:157-200, [S14] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go:74-78, [S30] /params/protocol_params.go:175-181

3. Blob pool performs additional checks: (a) sender account has sufficient balance for tx.cost = value + gasLimit * maxFeePerGas + blobGas * blobGasFeeCap where blobGas = len(blobs) * 131072, (b) nonce is exactly next expected nonce (no gaps allowed for blob txs per pool policy), (c) at most 16 blob txs per account, (d) no conflicting lower-nonce non-blob txs for same sender. [S13] [S14] Sources: [S13] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go:164-200, [S14] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go:80-86

4. Blob transaction with sidecar is written to persistent storage (billy database in datadir/blobpool/queue). [S13] [S31] Only metadata kept in memory to save RAM. [S13] Sources: [S13] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go:164-200, [S31] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go:88-98
5. Blob transaction hash is announced to peers (blobs not broadcast, pull-only per EIP-4844 design). [S13] [S27] Sources: [S13] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go:164-200, [S27] /eth/handler.go
6. For post-Osaka fork, legacy blob transactions with old proof format are accepted within 2-hour conversion window, then rejected. [S32] Sources: [S32] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go:100-103

7. Blob tx replacement requires 100% fee bump (2x multiplier on maxFeePerGas, maxPriorityFeePerGas, and blobGasFeeCap) to discourage cancellations. [S13] Sources: [S13] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go:192-195

8. When included in block, blobs are attached to block for propagation to consensus layer. [S33] Blob gas usage (blobGasUsed) and excess blob gas tracked in block header per EIP-4844. [S22] Sources: [S33] /beacon/engine/types.go:119-138, [S22] /consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:93-127
postconditions: Blob transaction stored in persistent blob pool with sidecar, announced to network, ready for block inclusion with blob fee market pricing applied. [S13] [S22] Post-inclusion, blobs retained in limbo until finalized (15-18 days), then pruned. [S13] Sources: [S13] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go, [S22] /consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go, [S31] /core/txpool/blobpool/blobpool.go:92-94

user_flows.title: EIP-7702 Set Code Transaction (Type 0x4) Processing
preconditions: Network has activated Prague fork (EIP-7702). [S2] Transaction type 0x4 enabled. [S7] Sources: [S2] /params/config.go:63, [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go:85-86
steps: 1. Client submits set code transaction (type 0x4) via RPC with authorizationList field containing tuples of (chainId, address, nonce, yParity, r, s) authorizing code delegation. [S7] Sources: [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go:149-153

2. ValidateTransaction checks: (a) type 0x4 accepted after Prague, (b) at least one authorization tuple present, (c) intrinsic gas includes 12500 gas per authorization tuple (TxAuthTupleGas), (d) standard signature and nonce validation. [S7] [S34] Sources: [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go:85-86, [S34] /params/protocol_params.go:101
3. Transaction admitted to legacy pool (blob pool rejects set code transactions). [S7] Sources: [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go:149-153

4. During execution, EVM processes authorization list: for each tuple, if authorization signature is valid and authorizer nonce matches, authorizer's account code is set to delegation designation pointing to target address. [S35] Sources: [S35] /core/vm/eips.go:43-44
5. Subsequent calls in same transaction to authorizer address execute code from target address in authorizer's context (EIP-7702 delegation). [S35] Sources: [S35] /core/vm/eips.go:43-44
6. State changes committed if transaction succeeds; reverted if fails. [S9] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:144-204
postconditions: Authorized accounts have code delegation set, enabling smart contract wallet functionality at EOA addresses for remainder of transaction. [S35] Sources: [S35] /core/vm/eips.go

user_flows.title: Block Building via Engine API (engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV3, engine_getPayloadV3)
preconditions: Execution client paired with consensus client post-merge. [S4] Engine API authenticated via JWT. [S4] Consensus client has determined it's time to propose a block. [S5] Sources: [S4] /eth/catalyst/api.go:48-58, [S5] /beacon/engine/types.go
steps: 1. Consensus client calls engine_forkchoiceUpdatedV3 with forkchoiceState (headBlockHash, safeBlockHash, finalizedBlockHash) and payloadAttributes (timestamp, prevRandao, suggestedFeeRecipient, withdrawals, parentBeaconBlockRoot). [S4] [S5] Sources: [S4] /eth/catalyst/api.go, [S5] /beacon/engine/types.go:55-65
2. Engine API updates fork choice state, sets new head if different from current. [S4] If payload attributes provided, initiates block building. [S4] Sources: [S4] /eth/catalyst/api.go
3. Miner.generateWork called with generateParams extracted from payload attributes. [S36] Parent block identified by headBlockHash. [S36] Sources: [S36] /miner/worker.go:118-188

4. prepareWork creates environment with: (a) parent header retrieved, (b) new header constructed with number = parent.number + 1, timestamp from CL, coinbase = suggestedFeeRecipient, difficulty = 0 (post-merge), mixDigest = prevRandao, (c) base fee calculated via EIP-1559 CalcBaseFee(parent), (d) excess blob gas calculated via EIP-4844 CalcExcessBlobGas(parent), (e) state database cloned from parent, (f) withdrawals validated against max size. [S21] [S22] [S36] Sources: [S21] /consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go:56-98, [S22] /consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:129-168, [S36] /miner/worker.go:193-295

5. Pre-execution system calls executed: (a) ProcessBeaconBlockRoot if beaconRoot provided (EIP-4788), (b) ProcessParentBlockHash for block history (EIP-2935) if Prague active. [S9] [S10] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:220-242, [S10] /core/state_processor.go:244-272

6. fillTransactions selects transactions from pool: (a) orders by effective tip (descending) and nonce (ascending), (b) includes transactions while gasPool available and under block size limit (MaxBlockSize - buffer), (c) blob transactions limited by MaxBlobsPerBlock for current fork (3 for Cancun, 6 for Osaka, 9 for BPO2), (d) validates each tx state-dependent requirements (balance, nonce), (e) executes via EVM, collects receipts. [S37] [S29] [S38] Sources: [S37] /miner/worker.go:134-145, [S29] /miner/ordering.go, [S38] /params/protocol_params.go:185

7. Post-execution system calls if Prague active: (a) ParseDepositLogs from receipts (EIP-6110), (b) ProcessWithdrawalQueue (EIP-7002), (c) ProcessConsolidationQueue (EIP-7251). [S39] [S40] [S41] Requests hash computed and set in header. [S37] Sources: [S39] /core/state_processor.go:323-335, [S40] /core/state_processor.go:274-278, [S41] /core/state_processor.go:280-284, [S37] /miner/worker.go:152-173
8. Consensus engine (beacon in post-merge) finalizes block with Finalize and FinalizeAndAssemble, computing final state root, receipts root, logs bloom. [S37] Sources: [S37] /miner/worker.go:175-178
9. Payload ID generated and returned in forkchoice response. [S4] Block building continues in background. [S37] Sources: [S4] /eth/catalyst/api.go, [S37] /miner/worker.go

Engine returns ExecutionPayloadEnvelope with executionPayload (block header + body), blockValue (total fees), blobsBundle (sidecars for blob txs), executionRequests (deposit/withdrawal/consolidation requests). [S4] [S5] Block includes system contract calls, user transactions, and consensus layer requests. [S37] Sources: [S4] /eth/catalyst/api.go, [S5] /beacon/engine/types.go, [S37] /miner/worker.go

user_flows.title: Payload Validation and Execution (engine_newPayloadV3)
preconditions: Consensus client received block from peer or built locally. [S4] Execution client has parent block and state. [S12] Sources: [S4] /eth/catalyst/api.go, [S12] /core/block_validator.go
steps: 1. Consensus client calls engine_newPayloadV3 with ExecutableData containing all block fields (parentHash, stateRoot, receiptsRoot, logsBloom, prevRandao, blockNumber, gasLimit, gasUsed, timestamp, extraData, baseFeePerGas, blockHash, transactions, withdrawals, blobGasUsed, excessBlobGas). [S4] [S5] Sources: [S4] /eth/catalyst/api.go, [S5] /beacon/engine/types.go:74-94
2. Engine API constructs block from executable data, verifies blockHash matches block hash of reconstructed block. [S4] Sources: [S4] /eth/catalyst/api.go

3. Block validator performs stateless validation: (a) parent block exists, (b) block number = parent.number + 1, (c) timestamp > parent.timestamp, (d) gas limit within bounds (max change = parent.gasLimit / 1024), (e) gas used <= gas limit, (f) base fee correct per EIP-1559 formula, (g) if Cancun+, excessBlobGas and blobGasUsed present and correct per EIP-4844 formula, (h) extra data size <= 32 bytes. [S12] [S21] [S22] Sources: [S12] /core/block_validator.go, [S21] /consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go:30-53, [S22] /consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:93-127

4. State processor executes block: (a) loads parent state, (b) applies DAO fork if applicable, (c) creates EVM block context, (d) executes pre-execution system calls (beacon root, parent hash), (e) iterates transactions calling ApplyTransactionWithEVM for each, (f) collects receipts and logs, (g) executes post-execution system calls (deposits, withdrawals, consolidations) if Prague, (h) calls consensus engine Finalize. [S9] [S42] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:60-138, [S42] /core/state_processor.go:141-217

5. Each transaction execution: (a) converts tx to Message with sender recovered, (b) creates EVM tx context, (c) applies state transition via EVM.Call/Create, (d) deducts gas fees, (e) generates receipt with status, gas used, logs. [S42] For blob txs, receipt includes blobGasUsed and blobGasPrice. [S42] Sources: [S42] /core/state_processor.go:144-204
6. After all transactions, compare computed state root with provided stateRoot in payload. [S12] Compare receipts root with provided receiptsRoot. [S12] Sources: [S12] /core/block_validator.go

7. If validation and execution succeed and roots match, return PayloadStatusV1 with status VALID and latestValidHash set to blockHash. [S4] [S43] Sources: [S4] /eth/catalyst/api.go, [S43] /beacon/engine/types.go:156-161
8. If validation fails, return INVALID with validationError. [S4] [S43] If parent unknown, return SYNCING. [S4] Sources: [S4] /eth/catalyst/api.go, [S43] /beacon/engine/types.go:156-161
9. Valid block inserted into chain, state committed to database. [S4] Sources: [S4] /eth/catalyst/api.go
postconditions: Payload validated and executed, state updated, block inserted into local chain if valid, or rejected with error if invalid. [S4] [S12] Consensus client receives status and proceeds accordingly. [S43] Sources: [S4] /eth/catalyst/api.go, [S12] /core/block_validator.go, [S43] /beacon/engine/types.go

user_flows.title: Transaction Execution and State Transition
preconditions: Block is being executed with validated transactions. [S9] State at parent block loaded. [S9] Gas pool initialized with block gas limit. [S9] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:60-70
steps: 1. For each transaction in block, TransactionToMessage converts tx to EVM message, recovering sender address via signature. [S9] [S42] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:99, [S42] /core/state_processor.go:211-215
2. Set transaction context in state (tx hash, tx index). [S9] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:103
3. ApplyTransactionWithEVM called with message, gas pool, state, block context. [S42] Sources: [S42] /core/state_processor.go:144-204
4. EVM transaction start hook called if tracer configured. [S42] Sources: [S42] /core/state_processor.go:145-148
5. Create new EVM tx context with origin, gas price. [S42] Sources: [S42] /core/state_processor.go:154-161
6. Deduct intrinsic gas from message gas limit. [S42] Buy gas from sender (deduct gasLimit * gasPrice from balance, add to gas pool). [S42] Sources: [S42] /core/state_processor.go:162-171
7. Create snapshot for potential revert. [S42] Sources: [S42] /core/state_processor.go:172

8. Execute message via EVM: (a) if contract creation (to == nil), call EVM.Create to deploy contract code, (b) if contract call, call EVM.Call to execute target code. [S44] EVM executes opcodes, accessing state, consuming gas. [S44] Sources: [S44] /core/vm/evm.go

9. Handle execution result: (a) if error, revert snapshot, (b) compute gas refund (limited to usedGas / RefundQuotient per EIP-3529), (c) refund unused gas to sender, (d) pay coinbase: baseFee burned (not transferred), effectiveTip * gasUsed sent to coinbase. [S42] For blob txs, blob fee (blobGasUsed * blobBaseFee) burned. [S42] Sources: [S42] /core/state_processor.go:173-188

10. Create receipt with status (success/fail), cumulative gas used, logs, contract address if creation, bloom filter. [S42] For blob tx, include blobGasUsed and blobGasPrice. [S42] Sources: [S42] /core/state_processor.go:189-204
11. Append receipt to block receipts, append logs to all logs. [S9] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:109-110
12. EVM transaction end hook called if tracer configured. [S42] Sources: [S42] /core/state_processor.go:149-151
13. Continue to next transaction. [S9] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:98-111
postconditions: Transaction executed, state updated (or reverted on error), receipt generated, gas consumed from pool, fees distributed (base fee and blob fee burned, tips to coinbase). [S9] [S42] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go, [S42] /core/state_processor.go:144-204

user_flows.title: EIP-4788 Beacon Block Root Processing (System Transaction)
preconditions: Block has beaconRoot set in header (Cancun+ fork). [S9] Block processing started. [S9] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:90-92
steps: 1. Before processing user transactions, ProcessBeaconBlockRoot called with beaconRoot from block header. [S9] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:90-92
2. System call hook invoked if tracer configured. [S9] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:223-227

3. Construct system message: from = SystemAddress (0xffffff...fe), to = BeaconRootsAddress (0x000F3df6D732807Ef1319fB7B8bB8522d0Beac02), data = beaconRoot (32 bytes), gasLimit = 30M, gasPrice = 0, no value. [S9] [S8] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:229-237, [S8] /params/protocol_params.go:207-209
4. Set EVM tx context with system message. [S9] Add BeaconRootsAddress to access list (warm access). [S9] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:238-239

5. Call beacon roots contract at BeaconRootsAddress. [S9] Contract code (hardcoded in protocol) stores beaconRoot indexed by timestamp: storage[timestamp % HISTORY_BUFFER_LENGTH] = beaconRoot, storage[(timestamp % HISTORY_BUFFER_LENGTH) + HISTORY_BUFFER_LENGTH] = beaconRoot. [S8] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:240, [S8] /params/protocol_params.go:209
6. Finalize state changes (system call consumes no gas from block, always succeeds). [S9] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:241
7. System call end hook invoked if tracer configured. [S9] Sources: [S9] /core/state_processor.go:225-227
postconditions: Beacon block root stored in beacon roots contract at addresses derived from block timestamp, accessible to contracts via SLOAD for building beacon chain light clients in EVM. [S8] [S9] Sources: [S8] /params/protocol_params.go:207-209, [S9] /core/state_processor.go:220-242

algorithms.name: EIP-1559 Base Fee Calculation
algorithms.purpose: Adjust base fee per gas to target 50% block fullness, creating elastic block gas limit and predictable fee market. [S21] Sources: [S21] /consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go:56-98
algorithms.notes: Base fee can change by at most 12.5% per block (denominator = 8). Minimum base fee is 0 (floor), maximum 1 wei increase guaranteed if target exceeded. Integer division used throughout. [S21] [S23] Sources: [S21] /consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go, [S23] /params/protocol_params.go:133

algorithms.name: EIP-4844 Excess Blob Gas Calculation
algorithms.purpose: Compute excess blob gas for blob fee market, tracking deviation from target blob count per block to adjust blob gas price exponentially. [S22] Sources: [S22] /consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:129-168
algorithms.notes: Cancun target: 3 blobs, max 6. Osaka target: 3, max 6. BPO2 target: 3, max 9. Blob gas per blob = 131072 (128KB). Osaka introduces reserve price mechanism (EIP-7918) to dampen price swings. [S22] [S48] Sources: [S22] /consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go, [S48] /params/config.go:69-75

algorithms.name: EIP-4844 Blob Fee Calculation (Fake Exponential)
algorithms.purpose: Calculate blob gas price using exponential formula approximated via Taylor series to avoid overflow, implementing responsive pricing for blob space. [S22] Sources: [S22] /consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go:213-227
algorithms.complexity: O(k) where k is number of Taylor series terms until accumulator reaches zero, typically small
algorithms.notes: Provides exponential pricing avoiding native exponentiation (no overflow risk). UpdateFraction controls price sensitivity. Blob gas price minimum is 1 wei. [S22] [S30] Sources: [S22] /consensus/misc/eip4844/eip4844.go, [S30] /params/protocol_params.go:178

algorithms.name: Transaction Intrinsic Gas Calculation
algorithms.purpose: Compute minimum gas required for transaction before EVM execution, covering transaction metadata and data costs per EIP-2028, EIP-2930, EIP-3860. [S7] Sources: [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go:124-131
algorithms.complexity: O(n) where n = data length + access list length + auth list length
algorithms.notes: Must be computed before EVM execution. Transaction rejected if gas limit < intrinsic gas. Istanbul reduced non-zero byte cost from 68 to 16. Shanghai added init code word cost. [S7] [S28] [S49] Sources: [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go, [S28] /params/protocol_params.go:96, [S49] /params/protocol_params.go

algorithms.name: EIP-7623 Floor Data Gas Calculation (Prague)
algorithms.purpose: Enforce minimum gas cost for transaction data to prevent block size bloat from cheap calldata, introduced in Prague fork. [S7] Sources: [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go:132-141
algorithms.notes: Prague fork validation checks tx.Gas() >= FloorDataGas(tx.Data()) in addition to intrinsic gas check. Ensures non-zero bytes cost at least 40 gas each (vs 16 from EIP-2028), limiting block size bloat. [S7] [S50] Sources: [S7] /core/txpool/validation.go:132-141, [S50] /params/protocol_params.go:97-98

algorithms.name: Effective Gas Price and Tip Calculation (EIP-1559)
algorithms.purpose: Determine actual gas price paid by transaction and tip received by miner in EIP-1559 fee market. [S29] Sources: [S29] /miner/ordering.go
algorithms.notes: Used for transaction ordering in mempool and block building (highest tip first). Base fee is burned (removed from supply), tip rewards miner. Transaction fails if maxFeePerGas < baseFee. [S29] Sources: [S29] /miner/ordering.go

algorithms.name: Transaction Sorting for Block Building
algorithms.purpose: Order transactions by profitability and validity constraints for optimal block building under gas and size limits. [S29] Sources: [S29] /miner/ordering.go
algorithms.complexity: O(n log m) where n = total transactions, m = number of accounts
algorithms.notes: Maintains per-account nonce ordering (protocol requirement) while maximizing miner revenue. Blob transactions handled separately with blob gas limits. Greedy selection stops when gas limit or block size reached. [S29] [S37] Sources: [S29] /miner/ordering.go, [S37] /miner/worker.go:134-145

algorithms.name: EIP-2929 Access List Gas Accounting
algorithms.purpose: Track warm/cold storage access to charge higher gas for first access to account or storage slot per transaction, mitigating certain DoS vectors. [S51] Sources: [S51] /core/vm/eips.go:124-161
algorithms.complexity: O(1) per access (assuming hash map access list)
algorithms.notes: Introduced in Berlin fork. Access list can be pre-populated via EIP-2930 transaction type to make certain accesses warm from start (pay upfront cost). Affects SLOAD, SSTORE, BALANCE, EXTCODEHASH, EXTCODESIZE, EXTCODECOPY, CALL, CALLCODE, DELEGATECALL, STATICCALL. [S51] [S52] Sources: [S51] /core/vm/eips.go, [S52] /params/protocol_params.go:68-76

algorithms.name: EIP-2200 Net-Metered SSTORE Gas Calculation
algorithms.purpose: Refine SSTORE gas costs to account for net storage changes, enabling patterns like reentrancy guards while preventing gas underflow attacks. [S53] Sources: [S53] /core/vm/eips.go:118-122
algorithms.notes: Replaced by EIP-2929 in Berlin (adds access list logic). Refunds capped at gasUsed / RefundQuotient per EIP-3529 (quotient = 5, so max 20% refund). Sentry gas prevents reentrancy issues. [S53] [S54] [S55] Sources: [S53] /core/vm/eips.go, [S54] /params/protocol_params.go:54-66, [S55] /params/protocol_params.go:172-173

algorithms.name: Block Gas Limit Validation
algorithms.purpose: Ensure block gas limit changes stay within protocol bounds to prevent DoS and maintain network stability per EIP-1559. [S56] Sources: [S56] /consensus/misc/gaslimit.go
algorithms.notes: Post-London (EIP-1559), parent gas limit is adjusted by elasticity multiplier (2) before validation if parent is pre-London block. Miners/validators can vote to adjust gas limit within these bounds. [S21] [S56] Sources: [S21] /consensus/misc/eip1559/eip1559.go:33-41, [S56] /consensus/misc/gaslimit.go
